user_request: 시가지, 골목 / 밤 / 전봇대. 대형 쓰레기통. 고철. 건물은 총 3개. 1개는 1층 기계구조물, 2층 집과 연결 계단. 다른 1개는 폭이 좁고30% 기계. 나머지는 자유로운3층. 세 장. 기존 생성물이나 서로를 참조하지 않고 새로 생성.

variations.name: western_machine_house
variations.title: 서쪽 기계 주택 골목
variations.paving: broad dry charcoal asphalt with two large flat slate repairs; no intersection or parking markings
variations.palette: muted moss-green upper house A, warm-gray narrow building B, desaturated ochre building C

exits.type: open pedestrian alley between building C and building A; no overhead lintel
fully retracted sideways corrugated gate near the far right part of rear boundary

variations.scene: Place A prominently along the LEFT flank, B as a slim freestanding building at rear-right, and C as a compact THREE-STOREY corner tenement at the far rear. All three are distinct structures joined only by boundary walls/fencing where needed. A: its whole ground storey is a salvaged municipal pump-and-power station, with two large drum housings, grounded support columns and a heavy rectangular load-bearing deck. On that deck is a recognizable one-storey moss-green HOME, with a door and residential windows. A broad straight external stair hugs A's courtyard-facing side, with evenly repeated treads, a real top landing flush to the home's door, and supported rails; it occupies the edge zone, not the main path. B: exceptionally slender frontage; a full-height modular mechanical service spine takes approximately 30% of its visible overall building mass, while the remaining majority is narrow habitation with a separate grounded entrance. C: three clearly separated compact storeys with three window tiers, a closed ground-floor door, a shallow stepped-back upper storey and a low parapet. Rooftops A/B/C have distinct functional arrangements: low duct/service deck, one grouped vent and battery rack, and low laundry-drying frame plus energy/ventilation modules; plan approximately half of each roof footprint as functional elements with visible support. Large lidded dumpster and a sorted low heap of thick scrap rings and sheet metal sit in the outer front-left recess. One utility pole is beside the outer foot of the house stair, outside its access and both exit passages, with one white lamp and a few chunky cables kept above walking height. Ground section: broad foundation layers, one ceramic drain and a separate power conduit leading to the pump base; no repeating exposed pipe wallpaper.
variations.prompt:
Create ONE brand-new independent game-environment concept image. Use ONLY the five attached master/style references in their assigned roles and this scene specification. No prior generated scene or other variation is an input. One full diorama, not a triptych.

STRUCTURE MUST KEEP
Use a single strict ORTHOGRAPHIC parallel camera, elevated quarter view, shared XYZ axes for the ENTIRE scene. Build on one flat square ground slab in cubic virtual space. All same-world-axis edges of the base, paving, building footings, wall tops and level roofs remain parallel, with no perspective convergence or depth-based scaling. Four ground corners extruded downward by a constant depth; corresponding top/bottom corners have the same vertical displacement. Show BOTH planar front cut faces and the entire base with comfortable blank margin below the nearest corner and above the highest roof. No curved ground, bent kerbs, bevelled corner, extra facets or lens distortion. Architecture ground footprints and player-contact walls are orthogonal to common X/Y axes; L/T/U plans and rectangular setbacks allowed, no diagonal or rotated building footprints. Roof joins, load-bearing supports and stair/landing connections must be coherent. Do not copy the cameras from the references.
Exactly two functional exits: one through each adjacent rear boundary direction, about 11 and 1 o'clock. Their positions/forms are specified below; keep both approaches, turning spaces and open-state connections continuously unobstructed. The center is a broad readable walking/combat area. Boundary walls/fences fill other gaps to prevent a third rear route. Front ground cut faces are not exits. The three buildings are compact: target tallest roofline around 6.3m and low supported rooftop items; the requested three storeys must read clearly. Every building has a credible human-scale door/shutter; decorative entrances remain closed unless assigned as an exit. On EACH building roof place purposeful functional equipment/props/architecture across approximately 40–80% of its footprint with support/connections and broad surface still visible. Roof occupancy is separate from the requested mechanical building fraction.

CURRENT SCENE
Urban district, alley at NIGHT. EXACTLY THREE buildings, with distinct roles A/B/C (do not render letters). Place A prominently along the LEFT flank, B as a slim freestanding building at rear-right, and C as a compact THREE-STOREY corner tenement at the far rear. All three are distinct structures joined only by boundary walls/fencing where needed. A: its whole ground storey is a salvaged municipal pump-and-power station, with two large drum housings, grounded support columns and a heavy rectangular load-bearing deck. On that deck is a recognizable one-storey moss-green HOME, with a door and residential windows. A broad straight external stair hugs A's courtyard-facing side, with evenly repeated treads, a real top landing flush to the home's door, and supported rails; it occupies the edge zone, not the main path. B: exceptionally slender frontage; a full-height modular mechanical service spine takes approximately 30% of its visible overall building mass, while the remaining majority is narrow habitation with a separate grounded entrance. C: three clearly separated compact storeys with three window tiers, a closed ground-floor door, a shallow stepped-back upper storey and a low parapet. Rooftops A/B/C have distinct functional arrangements: low duct/service deck, one grouped vent and battery rack, and low laundry-drying frame plus energy/ventilation modules; plan approximately half of each roof footprint as functional elements with visible support. Large lidded dumpster and a sorted low heap of thick scrap rings and sheet metal sit in the outer front-left recess. One utility pole is beside the outer foot of the house stair, outside its access and both exit passages, with one white lamp and a few chunky cables kept above walking height. Ground section: broad foundation layers, one ceramic drain and a separate power conduit leading to the pump base; no repeating exposed pipe wallpaper.
Paving: broad dry charcoal asphalt with two large flat slate repairs; no intersection or parking markings. Palette: muted moss-green upper house A, warm-gray narrow building B, desaturated ochre building C. 
Rear-left exit: open pedestrian alley between building C and building A; no overhead lintel. Rear-right exit: fully retracted sideways corrugated gate near the far right part of rear boundary. Stair is a domestic entrance to A's second floor and does not create a third map exit. Keep its access separate from the two protected passageways.

ART / REFERENCE ROLES — THIS TEST ONLY
Night, readable cool shadow masses and localized WHITE practical lamps. Lighting describes large planar forms; avoid hiding the exits or base under darkness, bloom or fog. Keep the road DRY; do not automatically add puddles. All architecture, utility pole, dumpster and scrap belong to Salvage Cyberpunk: advanced recovered machinery, adapter joints, replaced casings and purposeful repairs, with varied simple retro industrial controls and functional large mechanical forms. No green CRT. No characters, vehicles, phone booth, guardhouse, bicycles, comparison labels or unrequested extra buildings.
Render clean, broad, calm base-color planes on walls, paving and machinery. Leave most of each surface uninterrupted. On SELECTED intact areas add a few LARGE sparse brush marks and irregular flat pigment patches in nearby hues/values, with long-stroke direction following the surface. These color variations also occur on UNDAMAGED paint; they are not all rust, dirt or peeling. Restrict large repaired/damaged areas to a few believable places. Preserve material distinction and clear silhouettes without miniature dust or dense greebles.
The brush marks are flat COLOR, not physical relief. No embossed brush ridges, wavy contour tracing, broken-glass ripple texture, tiny mosaic rectangles, stippling, granular noise or global canvas pattern. Avoid painting every empty area with marks; keep quiet base-color space and a few broad tonal strokes. Ground should feel flat and matte. Show volume through grouped light/shadow, not microtexture. Do not turn the requested understated brush finish into uniformly smooth plastic or a featureless single-color fill.
Image 1, M01-01: full square diorama framing and two front cut faces ONLY. Exclude its perspective, commercial neon theme, exact buildings, props and markings.
Image 2, M02-01: two perpendicular rear blocking directions, two functional exits and clear connected center ONLY. Exclude diagram colors, fixed gate coordinates, icons, text and arrows.
Image 3, M03-10: large clean wall planes, selective material information and grouped light/shadow. Exclude source buildings, characters, UI, text, camera and street layout.
Image 4, M04-02: heavy functional mechanical masses, repaired broad painted housings, joints and structural assembly translated into environmental machinery ONLY. No character, limbs, face, humanoid robot or source photoreal surface density.
Image 5, user brush/light reference: broad quiet painted architecture surfaces with sparse large neighboring-tone brush patches, especially its cream facades; simple light/shadow masses. Apply that material treatment under the requested NIGHT lighting. Exclude source buildings, giant legs, harbor, boats, people, setting, perspective and daytime sky.
Do not add any text overlays, arrows, UI, watermarks or frames. Deliver one complete coherent landscape 4:3 diorama.

variations.name: eastern_power_house
variations.title: 동쪽 발전 주택 골목
variations.paving: large flat warm-gray concrete fields with a single straight darker service trench cover; sparse broad painted tone patches
variations.palette: dusty blue upper house A, faded brick-coral slender building B, warm ivory three-storey building C

exits.type: open gated alley between narrow B and three-storey C; gate leaves secured outside clearance
rectangular through-passage beneath house A through its mechanical ground level; open toward the rear-right edge

variations.scene: This layout puts A across the RIGHT rear flank and the tall C at the LEFT foreground edge, leaving the center visible. B is the pencil-width building at the far rear-left. A has a full ground-storey recovered electrical substation, with broad generator cassettes, switch housings and structural steel piers. A straight rectangular WALK-THROUGH opening passes through the center of this mechanical ground storey, forming the sole right-rear exit; the housings and support piers flank this passage and the second-floor home's load-bearing deck spans it. Its dusty blue second floor is unmistakably a HOUSE with domestic windows and an entrance. A two-flight external dogleg stair stands against the right courtyard-facing end of A, with a generous rectangular mid-landing and a second-floor landing reaching that house door; every tread/landing is supported, with no broken connections. B has a very narrow facade, two modest levels, a closed grounded door and an integrated side bank of vertical transformer/vent modules totaling about 30% of its overall visible building mass. C is a small three-storey residential repair building with three visible floor/window tiers, an offset rectangular third floor and a closed ground-floor repair-shop shutter; use a shallow asymmetric roof section joined coherently to a service terrace. Keep three separate building identities. Purposeful roof coverage about half per building: A low water-heater and ventilation deck; B a slim rooftop service rack; C low ducting, a hinged maintenance hatch and grouped solar/energy equipment on properly leveled supports. One large charcoal dumpster with a repaired motorized lid and several thick scrap panels/hubs are placed at the RIGHT outer edge, clear of the passage under A. One utility pole and white lamp stand near the left outer forecourt, outside the main route. Ground cuts use broad concrete foundation segments, an electrical service duct and a large sump pipe, with enough exposed earth to read the planar cut.

variations.name: rear_compressor_house
variations.title: 뒤쪽 압축기 주택 골목
variations.paving: oversized dry blue-gray stone/concrete paving slabs with straight sparse seams, each slab mostly one calm flat tone
variations.palette: warm bone upper house A above dark petrol machinery, muted plum slender building B, desaturated blue-gray three-storey C

exits.type: open side alley between A and B with a withdrawn mesh gate flat against boundary
uncovered rear alley between A and C, framed by the two buildings rather than a standalone door

variations.scene: Make a broken U-shaped arrangement of EXACTLY THREE separate buildings, with a wide open forecourt: house-over-machinery A at the REAR CORNER, narrow B along the LEFT side, and tall C along the RIGHT rear side, with two clear gaps at the two designated exits. A: an entirely mechanical first storey of recovered industrial air compressors, two squat horizontal pressure drums, large ribbed electrical housings and structural piers carrying a clear flat deck. Its second floor is a compact warm-bone residential house with a small low-pitch gabled roof, home windows and a normal human door. An external straight stair runs sideways along A's front face in the ground X direction, ending on a rectangular landing at the second-floor door; show its ground start, supported stringers and top connection clearly. The mechanical level remains floor one, the home floor two. B is a very narrow muted-plum building with a modest entrance and a deep but slim footprint; a vertical side cut-in filled by a repaired lift/power assembly forms about 30% of the overall visible building volume. C is a three-storey blue-gray building with three unmistakable stacked residential levels, a closed ground-floor doorway, a recessed second-floor balcony and a right-angle stepped roof terrace. Keep each silhouette distinct. Functional roof occupation approximately half per building: A a raised level maintenance cradle with water cylinder, flue and duct connection on one roof side; B low fan/service modules; C grouped mechanical ventilation plus a small clothesline/pergola frame, preserving roof surface between groups. Put one large industrial dumpster and a low pile of thick scrap tubes and bent body panels along the RIGHT edge well outside the rear alley route. A single utility pole with white lamp is off the left edge of the forecourt. Front cuts expose broad compacted earth, concrete pads under each structure and a large heat-supply pipe with one access chamber; no basement entrance.
